title: Sordland/Turn04/InT_SSCHighwayIssue
description: Half of the first infrastructure project has been completed. But further progress has been halted due to an issue which the player must choose to solve in a way. The player enters a meeting in Lenkurg. Dependant on each corporation a different issue appears and all of them have different absolute solutions or failures leading to making the opening deadline or missing it by two months.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "But the main purpose of our visit w..."
entries.dialogueText: But the main purpose of our visit was to solve construction issues that began to endanger the deadline.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "The H-3 Highway construction create..."
entries.dialogueText: The H-3 Highway construction created a second opportunity to visit the seaside town of Lenkurg known for its salmon. Thousands of people from the city were employed for construction work by the new highway project.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "There also was a message of support..."
entries.dialogueText: There also was a message of support from the mayor of Arvory, Eric Niel, who was grateful for the H-3 investments.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "The mayor welcomed us to his own ma..."
entries.dialogueText: The mayor welcomed us to his own mansion and praised us for our decision to extensively invest in the Agnland region.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "We first met with the mayor and too..."
entries.dialogueText: We first met with the mayor and took a brief tour in the city.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "The meeting ended. The three of us..."
entries.dialogueText: The meeting ended. The three of us went to the beach of Lenkurg. It was rather rocky, but very pristine. The sunset looked absolutely astonishing over the Markian Sea.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "The day-long visit ended with a din..."
entries.dialogueText: The day-long visit ended with a dinner involving the most important people in the city. Many of them were bureaucrats.

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“That should be it. Good that we ha..."
entries.dialogueText: “That should be it. Good that we have figured out a way to move the process forward.”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Later, we made our way back to Hols..."
entries.dialogueText: Later, we made our way back to Holsord.

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: GameCondition.Turn04_InT_Issue = true

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Afterwards, we gathered at the city..."
entries.dialogueText: Afterwards, we gathered at the city hall. Symon had a worried look on his face.

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: "“Trust me Mr. President this is the..."
entries.dialogueText: “Trust me Mr. President this is the best investment we could have done. The SSC will only grow and learn from this.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“This extra investment could be jus..."
entries.dialogueText: “This extra investment could be just enough to get things back on track. However, it is unfortunate we had to spend more because we need it elsewhere too.”

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: "“I'm not so sure what a warning can..."
entries.dialogueText: “I'm not so sure what a warning can do to the situation on the ground. The managers already have many issues to tackle.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“The state owns the SSC. They can't..."
entries.dialogueText: “The state owns the SSC. They can't retaliate and bite off the hand that feeds them.”
entries.menuText: “The state owns the SSC. They can't retaliate and bite off the hand that feeds them.”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Symon took a deep breath and contin..."
entries.dialogueText: Symon took a deep breath and continued.

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: "“With more resources the managers a..."
entries.dialogueText: “With more resources the managers are more likely to hit the deadline. Any other action just hurts Sordland.”

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: "“This was a bad decision. This hurt..."
entries.dialogueText: “This was a bad decision. This hurts the honorable SSC more than anything and will hamper our efforts.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“Couldn't agree more. This shouldn'..."
entries.dialogueText: “Couldn't agree more. This shouldn't keep going on any longer.”

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: "“I stand in agreement. The construc..."
entries.dialogueText: “I stand in agreement. The construction speed can recover if they expand the workforce and buy new machinery.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Give more money to the constructio..."
entries.dialogueText: “Give more money to the construction managers so they can hire more workers and buy machinery to hit the deadline.”
entries.menuText: “Give more money to the construction managers so they can hire more workers and buy machinery to hit the deadline.” [-1 Government Budget]

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Replace the construction managers..."
entries.dialogueText: “Replace the construction managers with more competent people to ensure the deadline is hit.”
entries.menuText: “Replace the construction managers with more competent people to ensure the deadline is hit.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Warn the construction managers. Se..."
entries.dialogueText: “Warn the construction managers. Send a formal warning from the Ministry of Economy and the Presidency.”
entries.menuText: “Warn the construction managers. Send a formal warning from the Ministry of Economy and the Presidency.”

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: "“It is very important that we creat..."
entries.dialogueText: “It is very important that we create jobs for our own citizens who are unemployed rather than foreigners.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“We can either give the constructio..."
entries.dialogueText: “We can either give the construction managers money, warn them or replace them.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“A cash injection would increase th..."
entries.dialogueText: “A cash injection would increase the project costs even further.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“One way or another we have to solv..."
entries.dialogueText: “One way or another we have to solve this issue. This can lead to real complications down the line otherwise.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“It might even be necessary for us..."
entries.dialogueText: “It might even be necessary for us to hit the opening date.”
entries.menuText: “It might even be necessary for us to hit the opening date.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“There is a good chance that they w..."
entries.dialogueText: “There is a good chance that they will take it far more seriously and take measures to increase speed.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“There is also the chance that the..."
entries.dialogueText: “There is also the chance that the money could be wasted. We already spent so much on this investment.”
entries.menuText: “There is also the chance that the money could be wasted. We already spent so much on this investment.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Giving them a serious warning coul..."
entries.dialogueText: “Giving them a serious warning could be the solution. A slap on the wrist can do wonders.”
entries.menuText: “Giving them a serious warning could be the solution. A slap on the wrist can do wonders.”

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: "“The state warning the state doesn'..."
entries.dialogueText: “The state warning the state doesn't make any sense at all anyway. Their reasons are just.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Officially warning them is a possi..."
entries.dialogueText: “Officially warning them is a possibility but isn't tangible, we need action.”
entries.menuText: “Officially warning them is a possibility but isn't tangible, we need action.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“I can only hope that they handle t..."
entries.dialogueText: “I can only hope that they handle the money well if they do get it. I'm still not fully convinced.”

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: "“If we make the opening ceremony on..."
entries.dialogueText: “If we make the opening ceremony on time the public will cherish our efficiency.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“It's good to see that failure isn'..."
entries.dialogueText: “It's good to see that failure isn't rewarded and punished. We will find more competent people through our networks.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“It would be a drastic measure but..."
entries.dialogueText: “It would be a drastic measure but not unreasonable. Replacing them with competent managers would do.”

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: "“You see that the likes of Underhal..."
entries.dialogueText: “You see that the likes of Underhall are willing to bend the rules and risk the lives of their workers to hit deadlines. The SSC abides by the rules and regulations.”

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: "“I disagree completely. The SSC man..."
entries.dialogueText: “I disagree completely. The SSC managers are the most experienced construction managers in Sordland.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Finding competent managers could w..."
entries.dialogueText: “Finding competent managers could work. New blood can move things back on track.”
entries.menuText: “Finding competent managers could work. New blood can move things back on track.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“We have a lot of talented construc..."
entries.dialogueText: “We have a lot of talented construction managers in the private industry who would work for us in the SSC.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“I have concerns about the construc..."
entries.dialogueText: “I have concerns about the construction due to progress being slower than expected.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“The SSC might need more resources..."
entries.dialogueText: “The SSC might need more resources to speed things up. That deadline must be met.”
entries.menuText: “The SSC might need more resources to speed things up. That deadline must be met.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“We scheduled the project to finish..."
entries.dialogueText: “We scheduled the project to finish in late 1955 but the Sordish State Corporation might miss that target with the current trajectory.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“We can't let mismanagement delay t..."
entries.dialogueText: “We can't let mismanagement delay the project. It is unacceptable.”
entries.menuText: “We can't let mismanagement delay the project. It is unacceptable.”

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: "“The SSC is an organisation of prin..."
entries.dialogueText: “The SSC is an organisation of principle so they aren't rushing and risking peoples lives. The state can't be reckless.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“The managers should be fired. This..."
entries.dialogueText: “The managers should be fired. This is unacceptable.”
entries.menuText: “The managers should be fired. This is unacceptable.”

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: "“But with that comes other issues...."
entries.dialogueText: “But with that comes other issues. We don't want to create chaos in the management team which could create further problems.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“I trust that the SSC will accompli..."
entries.dialogueText: “I trust that the SSC will accomplish it in time.”
entries.menuText: “I trust that the SSC will accomplish it in time.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“How can we increase the constructi..."
entries.dialogueText: “How can we increase the construction speed, Symon?”
entries.menuText: “How can we get the construction back on schedule?”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“That is the million ren question...."
entries.dialogueText: “That is the million ren question. There are a couple of issues that need to be resolved if we want the SSC to make the deadline.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“The warning will hopefully have a..."
entries.dialogueText: “The warning will hopefully have a positive result to their performance. We could escalate further later.”

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: "“Why would they? The SSC respects t..."
entries.dialogueText: “Why would they? The SSC respects the authorities fully. They would never dare to go against us.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“One of the important issues is the..."
entries.dialogueText: “One of the important issues is their construction management team. The other could be the outdated construction methods used which require more manpower, but we aren't sure if that contributes to the issue.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: BaseGame.Turn04_InT_HighwayIssue_Solved = true

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“I don't care about principles, our..."
entries.dialogueText: “I don't care about principles, our agreed opening dates must be met.”
entries.menuText: “I don't care about principles, our agreed opening dates must be met.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“This doesn't raise confidence at a..."
entries.dialogueText: “This doesn't raise confidence at all. Maybe we shouldn't have picked the SSC.”
entries.menuText: “This doesn't raise confidence at all. Maybe we shouldn't have picked the SSC.”

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: "“We shouldn't be risking lives, Mr...."
entries.dialogueText: “We shouldn't be risking lives, Mr. President. The SSC wouldn't slow construction down if it wasn't absolutely necessary.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“Either way we need them to solve t..."
entries.dialogueText: “Either way we need them to solve the issue at hand.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“Worth considering because I'm not..."
entries.dialogueText: “Worth considering because I'm not confident that they will hit their targets.”

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: "“I think so too but maybe we should..."
entries.dialogueText: “I think so too but maybe we should increase their budget to help them buy new machinery to speed up the process.”

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: "“After engaging with the managers,..."
entries.dialogueText: “After engaging with the managers, they have said that they are moving forward slowly but steadily. The cliff-side ground-laying construction between Lenkurg and Arvory is proving more dangerous than expected.”
